---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Liquidity-Covered Financing Discretion
EXPRESSION: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Repurchases should confirm cheapness more strongly when cash exceeds current debt, while issuance under the same liquidity cushion is more likely discretionary market timing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The conditioner measures liquid coverage of near-term obligations rather than low current debt alone, distinguishing firms that can finance actions without refinancing pressure. Continuous industry ranks preserve coverage and test whether the maturity result reflects genuine liquidity capacity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Profitability-Weighted Financing Conviction
EXPRESSION: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Financing choices should reveal more about valuation when positive profitability makes them discretionary rather than responses to operating distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Profitable cheap firms repurchasing shares receive the strongest confirmation, while profitable expensive issuers receive the largest financing penalty. Loss firms retain their book-to-market signal but receive little financing adjustment, reducing contamination from distressed issuance and unsustainable buybacks.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Continuously Flexible Payout Timing
EXPRESSION: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dvt, at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Repurchases and issuance should be more informative when low regular-dividend commitments give management greater freedom to time equity transactions.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The prior binary dividend screen performed well but passed much of the zero-dividend cross-section, making the conditioner nearly inactive. A continuous industry rank distinguishes degrees of payout flexibility while retaining the broad coverage and continuous portfolio composition associated with the successful additive design.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Debt-Increase-Only Repurchase Quality
EXPRESSION: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), MAX(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at), SUB(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap firms repurchasing without increasing debt should outperform, while new debt used alongside equity retirement should weaken the undervaluation signal.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The positive-part debt adjustment penalizes only debt increases, unlike prior net-external-financing constructions that also reward debt repayment and can therefore be driven by pure deleveraging. This isolates the funding quality of the equity action while retaining continuous valuation and financing legs.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Soft Two-Sided Financing Timing
EXPRESSION: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(ADD(MUL(MAX(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), SUB(ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), MUL(MIN(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), SUB(ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Repurchases should receive greater weight as firms become cheaper, whereas issuance should receive a larger penalty as firms become more expensive.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Positive and negative financing flows are separately weighted by cheapness and expensiveness ranks, creating the intended two-sided interaction without hard valuation cutoffs or event-only portfolios. The continuous valuation base and standardized interaction leg are designed to avoid the negative portfolio alpha observed for gross action-specific tails.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Asymmetric Deleveraging Confirmation
EXPRESSION: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(ADD(MIN(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), SUB(ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)))), MUL(MAX(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), SUB(ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)), ABS(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at)))), INDICATOR(NEG(LAG(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), 1)), 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Repurchases should be rewarded only after prior deleveraging, while equity issuance should remain adverse even when the firm did not previously reduce debt.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This preserves the successful temporal sequencing mechanism but fixes its asymmetric weakness: the issuance penalty is never suppressed, whereas the repurchase benefit requires prior debt reduction. The continuous book-to-market leg maintains broad portfolios despite the conditional treatment of positive financing flows.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Profitability-Weighted Financing Conviction---
VERDICT: flag

RATIONALE: Same archived additive-interaction template with profitability substituted as the conditioner, which both amounts to a value-plus-quality-plus-payout composite (well-trodden ground) and contradicts its own hypothesis, since IND_RANK(ib/at) does not isolate "positive profitability" and can assign high weights to loss-making firms in weak industries.

---CRITIQUE Continuously Flexible Payout Timing---

RATIONALE: A purely cosmetic binary-to-continuous recoding of the archived Flexible-Payout Value Timing signal within the archived Maturity-Weighted structure; no new economic mechanism is introduced and the resulting signal will be nearly collinear with both predecessors.

---CRITIQUE Debt-Increase-Only Repurchase Quality---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The positive-part debt adjustment is a well-motivated and correctly implemented fix (MAX(x, ABS(x)−ABS(x)) = max(x,0)) that isolates debt-funded repurchases from pure deleveraging, distinguishing it economically from the archived MIN-based Balance-Sheet-Safe Retirement, though it remains adjacent to known net-external-financing anomalies.
